column10: A 3 days old male patient brought to the clinic with the complaints of Bulging forehead. On examination bulging fontanelle and temperature 38.2°c.
column12:
Emergency Assessment
Bulging fontanelle with fever suggests meningitis, encephalitis, or increased intracranial pressure.

Immediate Treatment
Hospital Admission This is a medical emergency requiring urgent care.
IV Antibiotics Start empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., ampicillin + cefotaxime/gentamicin) for possible neonatal meningitis.
IV Fluids Maintain hydration and electrolyte balance.
Antipyretics Paracetamol for fever control.
Seizure Management If seizures occur, give anticonvulsants (e.g., phenobarbital).

Investigations
Lumbar puncture (CSF analysis) to confirm meningitis.
Blood cultures for infection.
Cranial ultrasound/CT scan if hydrocephalus or brain abscess is suspected.

Further Management & Follow-Up
Adjust antibiotics based on culture results.
Monitor for neurological complications (e.g., hydrocephalus, developmental delay).
